miniProject.title: Tabular sampling with exact trajectory oracles
miniProject.brief: Extend `policylab` with tabular Monte Carlo and TD control checked against fixed-trajectory oracles, plus behavior and target policy bookkeeping with support diagnostics. Every update is tested without environment noise before any multi-seed comparison runs.
steps: Add `tabular/` samplers that emit the shared trajectory record with environment, policy, seed and version identity, and reject records with missing identity before any update runs; evaluate only on held-out seed streams.

Build fixed-trajectory oracles for returns, one-step and multi-step targets that cut the bootstrap at termination and keep it at truncation, pass Deep-ML 272, Deep-ML 257 and Deep-ML 273, and catch seeded alignment and bootstrap defects.

Implement Sarsa, Expected Sarsa and Q-learning from explicit batches with no hidden environment calls, pass Deep-ML 175, Deep-ML 476 and Deep-ML 133, and label behavior against target policies on exploration-sensitive trajectories including a coverage failure.

Compute ordinary, weighted and per-decision importance estimates on fixed trajectories, track effective sample size curves and visitation logs that name uncovered pairs, and refuse estimates where support is missing.
Compare constant against decreasing step sizes under matched interaction budgets with visitation logs, and show which schedule tracks drift and which converges.

Run the Sarsa against Q-learning cliff comparison across several seeds with independent evaluation streams and matched budgets, pass Deep-ML 518, and derive the average-reward ring rate with its value gaps.
deliverables: Tabular samplers with the versioned trajectory schema and fixed-trajectory update oracles.
Tests: return and target boundaries, control updates, importance estimates, support refusal and seeded defects.
Matched-budget step-size and cliff comparisons with per-seed raw curves and the ring derivation.

checks.name: Deep-ML 272: First-Visit Monte Carlo Prediction
checks.note: Pass closed-book first; then add a two-episode average of your own.

checks.name: Deep-ML 257: Compute Temporal Difference Error
checks.note: Pass closed-book first; also test your own one-step value update.

checks.name: Deep-ML 273: n-Step TD Prediction
checks.note: Match the hand target first; add terminal-boundary cases of your own.

checks.name: Deep-ML 175: SARSA
checks.note: Match the chain by hand first; ties break toward the first action.

checks.name: Deep-ML 476: Expected SARSA
checks.note: Derive the expectation first; add a multi-step episode of your own.

checks.name: Deep-ML 133: Q-Learning
checks.note: Match the update and sampling order exactly; re-run on more seeds.

checks.name: Deep-ML 518: Cliff Walking Sarsa versus Q-Learning
checks.note: Treat pinned averages as regression values; report spread over more seeds.

rubric.pass: Fixed-trajectory returns and targets match hand computation, and every seeded alignment defect fails loudly.
rubric.strong: A live-run mismatch is traced to the update rather than blamed on sampling noise.

rubric.pass: Behavior and target policies are labeled on every trajectory, and the coverage failure refuses estimation.
rubric.strong: The cliff gap is attributed to update distribution rather than tuning.

rubric.pass: Visitation logs name uncovered pairs and effective sample size curves mark collapse.
rubric.strong: A planted zero-support pair is caught before any estimator runs.

rubric.pass: Comparisons use matched budgets with all seeds retained and evaluation on separate streams.
rubric.strong: A best-seed claim is shown to reverse under the full seed set.

miniProject.feedsInto: Tabular oracles, trajectory identity and support diagnostics feed deep value, policy, offline and language-policy projects and the capstone classical core.
